reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Every English line of the chapter was read against the Greek. No line adds interpretive content, uses Raëlian-canon vocabulary (no Elohim, Yahweh, craft, creators, ray, planet, Eternals), or resolves an ambiguity in the canon's direction. Each Wheel of Heaven reading sits in its own paragraph headed 'reception note, not a translation claim'. The two lines that coincide with the canon's French were tested specifically: 2:2/2:9 'at its rising' (BDAG ἀνατολή 1 cites both verses; NAB 1970, NRSV, ESV) and 26:53 'put at my disposal' (BDAG παρίστημι 1a cites the verse; NASB identical wording). reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts were formed from the Greek, the chapter JSON, the overlay and the central diff before the escalation report (wave-m2-editor-report.md) was opened. The report added no information that changes a verdict. It repeats the RSV attribution for 2:2/9 ('RSV, NRSV, NAB'), which this review corrects. Its ten founder-preference points are answered in founderDecisionRecommendations, and its follow-ups (17:21; 17:22; comma/colon in 25 and 28; the 6:13 'testing' wording in central) are endorsed as later-pass items.

founderDecisionRecommendations.1-angelos-angel: Endorse. ἄγγελος is the technical term for a heavenly envoy in first-century Jewish Greek (BDAG s.v. 2); published Mt 1, 13, 25, 28, Acts 12 and the Revelation wave all print 'angel', so the Greek NT is already harmonized in practice. Promote jointly with Revelation as a central Greek-NT convention; keep 'messenger of YHWH' for Hebrew malʾāḵ.
founderDecisionRecommendations.2-naos-sanctuary: Endorse for Matthew. The naos/hieron distinction is lexical (BDAG; Josephus) and NRSV marks it in 23:16-35. 27:5 keeps Matthew's crux honestly (and, to my reading, restores the ASV's own 'sanctuary'). If promoted, scope it to books with both terms; Revelation's 'temple' for ναός is defensible because it has no ἱερόν.
founderDecisionRecommendations.3-23:14-no-paragraph: Endorse. SBLGNT has no 23:14; the Byzantine text is quoted in full at 23:13 with witnesses, as the 6:13b precedent and the Revelation ruling C require. Recommend a later pass bring the stable 17:21 into line: its bracketed Greek is not SBLGNT text, so drop the paragraph and move the Byzantine wording into the 17:20 commentary.
founderDecisionRecommendations.4-colon-convention: Endorse (punctuation only; applied without exception in the wave). Harmonize published 25 and 28 in a later pass.
founderDecisionRecommendations.5-magi: Endorse. 'magi' is the standard scholarly rendering (BDAG; Brown; Powell) and NIV/NAB usage; 'wise men' is noted.
founderDecisionRecommendations.6-faithfulness-23:23: Endorse. BDAG lists Mt 23:23 under πίστις 1a 'faithfulness, reliability'; NIV and ESV render so; the Mic 6:8 triad is conduct.
founderDecisionRecommendations.7-put-at-my-disposal-26:53: Endorse. BDAG παρίστημι 1a cites this verse for 'put at someone's disposal', and the NASB prints exactly 'put at My disposal'; the ground is independent of the canon's French, and the coincidence is disclosed.
founderDecisionRecommendations.8-at-its-rising-2:2,9: Endorse. BDAG ἀνατολή 1 cites both verses; NAB (1970, before TBWTT) and NRSV read 'at its rising', ESV 'when it rose'. Correct the RSV attribution (the RSV reads 'in the East').
founderDecisionRecommendations.9-defiles-a-person: Endorse. The article with ἄνθρωπος is generic; the canon's own French « l'homme » is generic too, so the line follows the sense the canon intends rather than the English edition's 'the man'.

Agent-driven 'tempted'/'the tempter' is BDAG's and the versions' reading with the devil as agent, and agrees with published 6:13; the test reading (Gerhardsson; canon « mis à l'épreuve ») is properly in commentary. paragraphs.text: Τότε ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀνήχθη εἰς τὴν ἔρημον ὑπὸ τοῦ πνεύματος, πειρασθῆναι ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου.
paragraphs.translit: tote ho iēsous anēchthē eis tēn erēmon hypo tou pneumatos, peirasthēnai hypo tou diabolou.

i18n.en: Then Jesus was led up into the wilderness by the Spirit to be tempted by the devil.

notes.official:
*peirasthēnai hypo tou diabolou* 'to be tempted by the devil'. *peirazō* means both 'put to the test' and 'entice to do wrong' (BDAG s.v. 2, 4). With the devil as agent, and with *ho peirazōn* 'the tempter' in 4:3, the major versions render 'tempted'. The episode is also a test of the Son: Gerhardsson (The Testing of God's Son, 1966) reads it against Israel's forty years, during which God 'tested' Israel (Deut 8:2), and every reply of Jesus quotes Deut 6-8. The line keeps 'tempted' for agreement with 4:3 and with the published 6:13 ('temptation') (`peirazo-peirasmos-tempt-test-matthew`).

*ho diabolos* 'the devil': etymologically 'the slanderer' (from *diaballō* 'to slander, accuse'), the LXX word for the Hebrew *haśśāṭān* of Job 1-2 and Zech 3. In the Gospels it is a title, used interchangeably with the name 'Satan' (4:10) (`diabolos-the-devil-matthew`). *hypo tou pneumatos* 'by the Spirit' (`pneuma-spirit-capitalization-matthew`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 4) quotes 4:1 as « Alors Jésus fut emmené au désert (…) pour être mis à l'épreuve du diable » and reads the devil as Satan, one of the creators, opposed to the creation of humanity, who tests whether Jesus can be trusted. Let's Welcome the Extraterrestrials (ch. 2) quotes 4:1-11 in full as a test of Jesus' fidelity to the Elohim, and glosses *diabolos* as « calomniateur » ('slanderer'), which is the accurate etymology. This note covers the canon's citations of 4:1-11. The line keeps the standard renderings 'tempted' and 'the devil', and the 'test' and 'slanderer' senses are given above.

paragraphs.text: καὶ νηστεύσας ἡμέρας τεσσεράκοντα καὶ νύκτας τεσσεράκοντα ὕστερον ἐπείνασεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai nēsteusas hēmeras tesserakonta kai nyktas tesserakonta hysteron epeinasen.

i18n.en: And when he had fasted forty days and forty nights, afterward he was hungry.

notes.official: 'forty days and forty nights': Moses' fast on the mountain (Exod 34:28; Deut 9:9) and Elijah's journey to Horeb (1 Kgs 19:8). Matthew alone adds 'and forty nights', which matches the Moses texts.

paragraphs.text: καὶ προσελθὼν ὁ πειράζων εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Εἰ υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ θεοῦ, εἰπὲ ἵνα οἱ λίθοι οὗτοι ἄρτοι γένωνται.
paragraphs.translit: kai proselthōn ho peirazōn eipen autō· ei huios ei tou theou, eipe hina hoi lithoi houtoi artoi genōntai.

i18n.en: And the tempter came and said to him: "If you are the Son of God, command that these stones become loaves of bread."

notes.official:
*ho peirazōn* 'the tempter', the participle as a noun (`peirazo-peirasmos-tempt-test-matthew`). *Ei huios ei tou theou* 'If you are the Son of God': the condition assumes the truth of the voice of 3:17 and questions how the sonship will be used (`huios-theou-son-of-god-rendering-matthew`).

This verse is quoted in the canon; see the reception note at 4:1.

paragraphs.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Γέγραπται· Οὐκ ἐπʼ ἄρτῳ μόνῳ ζήσεται ὁ ἄνθρωπος, ἀλλʼ ἐπὶ παντὶ ῥήματι ἐκπορευομένῳ διὰ στόματος θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen· gegraptai· ouk epʼ artō monō zēsetai ho anthrōpos, allʼ epi panti rhēmati ekporeuomenō dia stomatos theou.

i18n.en: But he answered and said: "It is written: 'Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God.'"

notes.official:
Deut 8:3 LXX, verbatim. *ho anthrōpos* is collective and gnomic, so the English collective 'Man' (humankind) is kept (`anthropos-generic-people-convention-matthew`).

This verse is quoted in the canon; see the reception note at 4:1.

paragraphs.text: Τότε παραλαμβάνει αὐτὸν ὁ διάβολος εἰς τὴν ἁγίαν πόλιν, καὶ ἔστησεν αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸ πτερύγιον τοῦ ἱεροῦ,
paragraphs.translit: tote paralambanei auton ho diabolos eis tēn hagian polin, kai estēsen auton epi to pterygion tou hierou,

i18n.en: Then the devil takes him into the holy city, and he set him on the pinnacle of the temple,

notes.official: *epi to pterygion tou hierou* 'on the pinnacle of the temple': *pterygion* is literally 'little wing', a projecting part whose exact location is unknown. *to hieron* is the temple precinct as a whole, rendered 'temple'; *ho naos*, the sanctuary building, is rendered 'sanctuary' (23:16-21; 26:61; 27:5, 40, 51) (`naos-sanctuary-hieron-temple-matthew`).

paragraphs.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Εἰ υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ θεοῦ, βάλε σεαυτὸν κάτω· γέγραπται γὰρ ὅτι Τοῖς ἀγγέλοις αὐτοῦ ἐντελεῖται περὶ σοῦ καὶ ἐπὶ χειρῶν ἀροῦσίν σε, μήποτε προσκόψῃς πρὸς λίθον τὸν πόδα σου.
paragraphs.translit: kai legei autō· ei huios ei tou theou, bale seauton katō· gegraptai gar hoti tois angelois autou enteleitai peri sou kai epi cheirōn arousin se, mēpote proskopsēs pros lithon ton poda sou.

i18n.en: and says to him: "If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down; for it is written: 'He will give his angels charge concerning you,' and 'On their hands they will bear you up, lest you strike your foot against a stone.'"

notes.official:
Ps 91:11-12 (90:11-12 LXX), quoted by the devil. 'his angels' (`angelos-angel-matthew-convention`).

This verse is quoted in the canon; see the reception note at 4:1.

paragraphs.text: ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πάλιν γέγραπται· Οὐκ ἐκπειράσεις κύριον τὸν θεόν σου.
paragraphs.translit: ephē autō ho iēsous· palin gegraptai· ouk ekpeiraseis kyrion ton theon sou.

i18n.en: Jesus said to him: "Again it is written: 'You shall not make trial of the Lord your God.'"

notes.official:
Deut 6:16 LXX. *ekpeirazō* 'make trial of', the compound of *peirazō*: the devil's 'test' is answered with the command not to 'test' God (`peirazo-peirasmos-tempt-test-matthew`). *kyrion ton theon sou* 'the Lord your God' renders the LXX for YHWH ʾĕlōhêḵā.

This verse is quoted in the canon; see the reception note at 4:1.

paragraphs.text: Πάλιν παραλαμβάνει αὐτὸν ὁ διάβολος εἰς ὄρος ὑψηλὸν λίαν, καὶ δείκνυσιν αὐτῷ πάσας τὰς βασιλείας τοῦ κόσμου καὶ τὴν δόξαν αὐτῶν
paragraphs.translit: palin paralambanei auton ho diabolos eis oros hypsēlon lian, kai deiknysin autō pasas tas basileias tou kosmou kai tēn doxan autōn

i18n.en: Again the devil takes him to a very high mountain and shows him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory,

notes.official: *eis oros hypsēlon lian* 'to a very high mountain': the third scene is set on a mountain, like the Sermon (5:1), the Transfiguration (17:1) and the final commission (28:16) (`mountain-as-revelation-site-mt-cross-corpus-har-sinai-mount-sapunu`).

paragraphs.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ταῦτά σοι πάντα δώσω, ἐὰν πεσὼν προσκυνήσῃς μοι.
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen autō· tauta soi panta dōsō, ean pesōn proskynēsēs moi.

i18n.en: and he said to him: "All these things I will give you, if you will fall down and worship me."

notes.official:
*pesōn proskynēsēs moi* 'fall down and worship me': the verb that Jesus' reply in 4:10 reserves for God (`proskyneo-worship-kneel-matthew`).

This verse is quoted in the canon; see the reception note at 4:1.

paragraphs.text: τότε λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ὕπαγε, Σατανᾶ· γέγραπται γάρ· Κύριον τὸν θεόν σου προσκυνήσεις καὶ αὐτῷ μόνῳ λατρεύσεις.
paragraphs.translit: tote legei autō ho iēsous· hypage, satana· gegraptai gar· kyrion ton theon sou proskynēseis kai autō monō latreuseis.

i18n.en: Then Jesus says to him: "Go away, Satan! For it is written: 'You shall worship the Lord your God, and him only shall you serve.'"

notes.official:
*Hypage, Satana* 'Go away, Satan!': *Satanas* transliterates the Aramaic *sāṭānā* and is used as a personal name, here in the vocative without article (`satanas-satan-name-matthew`). The central `ha-satan` ('the adversary') governs the Hebrew word with the article in Job, a role title, and is not applied to the Greek name. The Byzantine majority text adds *opisō mou* 'behind me' (cf. 16:23); SBLGNT and the Textus Receptus (KJV 'Get thee hence, Satan') lack it.

Deut 6:13: most LXX manuscripts read *phobēthēsē* 'you shall fear'; Matthew has *proskynēseis* 'you shall worship', which answers the devil's demand of 4:9, and adds *monō* 'only'; Codex Alexandrinus of the LXX has both *proskynēseis* and *monō* (`proskyneo-worship-kneel-matthew`).

This verse is quoted in the canon; see the reception note at 4:1.

paragraphs.text: τότε ἀφίησιν αὐτὸν ὁ διάβολος, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄγγελοι προσῆλθον καὶ διηκόνουν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: tote aphiēsin auton ho diabolos, kai idou angeloi prosēlthon kai diēkonoun autō.

i18n.en: Then the devil leaves him, and behold, angels came and were ministering to him.

notes.official:
*angeloi prosēlthon kai diēkonoun autō* 'angels came and were ministering to him': the imperfect describes ongoing service, perhaps food after the fast (cf. 1 Kgs 19:5-8, where a messenger feeds Elijah) (`angelos-angel-matthew-convention`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** Let's Welcome the Extraterrestrials (ch. 2) reads the angels of this verse as 'the Elohim's messengers' (« les messagers des Elohim ») who come to complete Jesus' initiation once the test has been passed. 'Messenger' is the etymological sense of *angelos*; the line keeps the New Testament convention 'angels'.

paragraphs.text: Ἀκούσας δὲ ὅτι Ἰωάννης παρεδόθη ἀνεχώρησεν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν.
paragraphs.translit: akousas de hoti iōannēs paredothē anechōrēsen eis tēn galilaian.

i18n.en: Now when he heard that John had been handed over, he withdrew into Galilee.

notes.official: *paredothē* 'had been handed over': *paradidōmi* is the verb Matthew uses for John's arrest and for Jesus' betrayal and delivery (10:4; 26:2, 15-16; 27:2, 26). The program renders it 'hand over' throughout, rather than 'betray'.

paragraphs.text: καὶ καταλιπὼν τὴν Ναζαρὰ ἐλθὼν κατῴκησεν εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ τὴν παραθαλασσίαν ἐν ὁρίοις Ζαβουλὼν καὶ Νεφθαλίμ·
paragraphs.translit: kai katalipōn tēn nazara elthōn katōkēsen eis kapharnaoum tēn parathalassian en horiois zaboulōn kai nephthalim·

i18n.en: And leaving Nazareth, he came and dwelt in Capernaum, which is beside the sea, in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali,

paragraphs.text: ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἠσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος·
paragraphs.translit: hina plērōthē to rhēthen dia ēsaiou tou prophētou legontos·

i18n.en: so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, saying:

paragraphs.text: Γῆ Ζαβουλὼν καὶ γῆ Νεφθαλίμ, ὁδὸν θαλάσσης, πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, Γαλιλαία τῶν ἐθνῶν,
paragraphs.translit: gē zaboulōn kai gē nephthalim, hodon thalassēs, peran tou iordanou, galilaia tōn ethnōn,

i18n.en: "Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles —

notes.official: Isa 8:23-9:1 (EV 9:1-2), in a form close to neither the LXX nor the MT exactly. *Galilaia tōn ethnōn* 'Galilee of the Gentiles' anticipates the mission to 'all the nations' of 28:19.

paragraphs.text: ὁ λαὸς ὁ καθήμενος ἐν σκοτίᾳ φῶς εἶδεν μέγα, καὶ τοῖς καθημένοις ἐν χώρᾳ καὶ σκιᾷ θανάτου φῶς ἀνέτειλεν αὐτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: ho laos ho kathēmenos en skotia phōs eiden mega, kai tois kathēmenois en chōra kai skia thanatou phōs aneteilen autois.

i18n.en: the people who sat in darkness saw a great light, and to those who sat in the region and shadow of death, light dawned on them."

paragraphs.text: Ἀπὸ τότε ἤρξατο ὁ Ἰησοῦς κηρύσσειν καὶ λέγειν· Μετανοεῖτε, ἤγγικεν γὰρ ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.
paragraphs.translit: apo tote ērxato ho iēsous kēryssein kai legein· metanoeite, ēngiken gar hē basileia tōn ouranōn.

i18n.en: From that time Jesus began to preach and to say: "Repent, for the kingdom of the heavens has come near."

notes.official: 'Repent, for the kingdom of the heavens has come near': identical to John's proclamation at 3:2 (`kingdom-of-heaven-basileia-tōn-ouranōn-mt-distinctive-cross-corpus-hebrew-malkhut-shamayim`).

paragraphs.text: Περιπατῶν δὲ παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν τῆς Γαλιλαίας εἶδεν δύο ἀδελφούς, Σίμωνα τὸν λεγόμενον Πέτρον καὶ Ἀνδρέαν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, βάλλοντας ἀμφίβληστρον εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, ἦσαν γὰρ ἁλιεῖς·
paragraphs.translit: peripatōn de para tēn thalassan tēs galilaias eiden dyo adelphous, simōna ton legomenon petron kai andrean ton adelphon autou, ballontas amphiblēstron eis tēn thalassan, ēsan gar halieis·

i18n.en: And walking beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon who is called Peter and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea; for they were fishermen.

paragraphs.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Δεῦτε ὀπίσω μου, καὶ ποιήσω ὑμᾶς ἁλιεῖς ἀνθρώπων.
paragraphs.translit: kai legei autois· deute opisō mou, kai poiēsō hymas halieis anthrōpōn.

i18n.en: And he says to them: "Come after me, and I will make you fishers of people."

notes.official: *halieis anthrōpōn* 'fishers of people': generic plural *anthrōpoi*, rendered 'people' as in the published 5:13, 16 and 6:1-18 (`anthropos-generic-people-convention-matthew`). The ASV and KJV have 'fishers of men'. The image recalls Jer 16:16, where YHWH sends 'many fishers' to gather the people.

paragraphs.text: οἱ δὲ εὐθέως ἀφέντες τὰ δίκτυα ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de eutheōs aphentes ta diktya ēkolouthēsan autō.

i18n.en: And immediately they left the nets and followed him.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ προβὰς ἐκεῖθεν εἶδεν ἄλλους δύο ἀδελφούς, Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ μετὰ Ζεβεδαίου τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτῶν καταρτίζοντας τὰ δίκτυα αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐκάλεσεν αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: kai probas ekeithen eiden allous dyo adelphous, iakōbon ton tou zebedaiou kai iōannēn ton adelphon autou, en tō ploiō meta zebedaiou tou patros autōn katartizontas ta diktya autōn, kai ekalesen autous.

i18n.en: And going on from there he saw two other brothers, James the son of Zebedee and John his brother, in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them.

paragraphs.text: οἱ δὲ εὐθέως ἀφέντες τὸ πλοῖον καὶ τὸν πατέρα αὐτῶν ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de eutheōs aphentes to ploion kai ton patera autōn ēkolouthēsan autō.

i18n.en: And immediately they left the boat and their father and followed him.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ περιῆγεν ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ, διδάσκων ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αὐτῶν καὶ κηρύσσων τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς βασιλείας καὶ θεραπεύων πᾶσαν νόσον καὶ πᾶσαν μαλακίαν ἐν τῷ λαῷ.
paragraphs.translit: kai periēgen en holē tē galilaia, didaskōn en tais synagōgais autōn kai kēryssōn to euangelion tēs basileias kai therapeuōn pasan noson kai pasan malakian en tō laō.

i18n.en: And he went about in all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues and proclaiming the gospel of the kingdom and healing every disease and every sickness among the people.

notes.official: *kēryssōn to euangelion tēs basileias* 'proclaiming the gospel of the kingdom': *euangelion* means 'good news'. 'Gospel' is the English calque (Old English *gōdspel*) and the program's established rendering on the NT surface (Mk 16:15; Acts 15:7) (`euangelion-gospel-matthew`). The summary is repeated almost verbatim at 9:35, framing the Sermon (5-7) and the deeds (8-9).

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἀπῆλθεν ἡ ἀκοὴ αὐτοῦ εἰς ὅλην τὴν Συρίαν· καὶ προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ πάντας τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας ποικίλαις νόσοις καὶ βασάνοις συνεχομένους, δαιμονιζομένους καὶ σεληνιαζομένους καὶ παραλυτικούς, καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: kai apēlthen hē akoē autou eis holēn tēn syrian· kai prosēnenkan autō pantas tous kakōs echontas poikilais nosois kai basanois synechomenous, daimonizomenous kai selēniazomenous kai paralytikous, kai etherapeusen autous.

i18n.en: And the report of him went out into all Syria; and they brought to him all who were ill, afflicted with various diseases and torments, the demon-possessed and the moon-struck and paralytics; and he healed them.

notes.official:
*selēniazomenous* 'moon-struck', literally 'affected by the moon': ancient medicine linked seizures to the moon, and 'epileptic' (ASV, RSV) is an interpretation of the symptom. The literal rendering keeps the ancient diagnosis visible; the term recurs at 17:15, where the published line also reads 'moon-struck'. *daimonizomenous* 'demon-possessed'.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 4) quotes 4:24 (« on lui présenta tous les mal-portants… et il les soigna ») and reads Jesus' healings as the application of scientific teaching received from the creators, so that the people would rally to him. The line renders the Greek medical and possession vocabulary as written.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ ὄχλοι πολλοὶ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ Δεκαπόλεως καὶ Ἱεροσολύμων καὶ Ἰουδαίας καὶ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου.
paragraphs.translit: kai ēkolouthēsan autō ochloi polloi apo tēs galilaias kai dekapoleōs kai hierosolymōn kai ioudaias kai peran tou iordanou.

i18n.en: And great crowds followed him from Galilee and the Decapolis and Jerusalem and Judea and from beyond the Jordan.

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: πειράζω / πειρασθῆναι (peirazō; also ὁ πειράζων 'the tempter' 4:3; cf. 16:1, 19:3, 22:18, πειρασμός 26:41): 'tempt' vs. 'test'. The canon quotes 4:1 as « pour être mis à l'épreuve du diable » (to be put to the test) and LWTE ch. 2 reads the episode as a test of fidelity. The central Lord's-Prayer entry's wohChoice text says 'testing' for πειρασμός, but the stable precedent surface at 6:13 reads 'temptation'.
editorial_questions_resolved.default_taken: to be tempted by the devil
editorial_questions_resolved.resolution: 'to be tempted' / 'the tempter' kept (agent = devil; BDAG s.v. πειράζω 4; consistent with published 6:13 'temptation'); 'testing him' for opponents' questions (19:3); test reading (Gerhardsson) and canon « mis à l'épreuve » in commentary. Central Lord's-Prayer entry text ('testing') vs published 6:13 surface ('temptation') flagged for a later pass.

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: διάβολος (diabolos; also 4:5, 4:8, 4:11; precedent 13:39, 25:41): 'the devil' vs. the etymological 'the slanderer' / 'the accuser'. LWTE ch. 2 explicitly glosses diabolos as « calomniateur » (slanderer). No Greek-side glossary entry.
editorial_questions_resolved.resolution: 'the devil' kept as the title; etymology 'slanderer' and LWTE « calomniateur » in commentary.

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: Σατανᾶ (Satana, vocative): the central entry ha-satan renders Hebrew הַשָּׂטָן in Job as 'the adversary', but is scoped to Job; here the Greek is an anarthrous name in direct address, and the canon (LWTE ch. 2) treats it as a personal name. Also a minor variant: some Byzantine witnesses add ὀπίσω μου ('Get behind me'), absent from SBLGNT and from the KJV.
editorial_questions_resolved.resolution: 'Satan' kept as a personal name; central ha-satan (Hebrew, article, Job) not applied; Byzantine 'Get behind me' noted.

editorial_questions_resolved.issue: ἁλιεῖς ἀνθρώπων (halieis anthrōpōn): the precedent chapters render generic ἄνθρωποι as 'people' (5:13, 5:16, 6:1); the traditional phrase is 'fishers of men' (ASV/KJV).
editorial_questions_resolved.resolution: 'fishers of people' kept per the generic-anthrōpoi convention of the published chapters.
'gospel' kept, consistent with published Mk 16:15 and Acts 15:7; 'good news' in commentary.
